intro: You already compare things (**bigger than**, **as … as**) and link ideas (**whereas**, **Nevertheless,**, **Overall,**). Now you'll put them to work on numbers: say how figures **rise, fall, peak** and **fluctuate**, compare them precisely (**twice as high as**, **slightly lower than**), and write a graph report in **IELTS Writing Task 1** style. The app can't show real charts here, so every chart comes as a small table of figures.
teachingNotes: Chain recap, one line each, don't re-teach: a2-comparatives (-er / more … than, the -est / the most, as … as / not as … as; 'than', not 'from') and b2-linking-words (whereas / while + subject + verb to set two facts side by side; However, / Nevertheless, + a new sentence; Overall, to sum up). This is a writing lesson (strand WR) for study abroad, IELTS and work reports (sales, users, survey results). Since images can't be shown, every chart is given as a small table or a described line in the prompt: say so, and in the real exam the learner sees a picture. All figures in the lesson are practice figures, not real statistics: don't present them as facts about Indonesia.

Trend vocabulary. Up: rise (rose, risen), increase, grow (grew, grown), go up (went up). Down: fall (fell, fallen), decrease, decline, drop. Top: peak (at 400) / reach a peak (of 400). Flat: level off (BrE levelled, AmE leveled), remain stable / steady (at about 300). Up and down: fluctuate (between X and Y). Here these verbs are intransitive (no object): the node's common error *'The number of users was increase(d)' → 'The number of users increased.' Explain why: learners add 'was' as a past marker for 'sudah' (sudah meningkat → *was increase), but the past is already in -ed; and a chart line moves by itself, so no passive either. A passive is only possible when someone did it (The company increased its prices → Prices were increased by the company); in a chart report always use the active. rise vs raise: prices rose (no object) vs the company raised prices (+ object). Teach the irregular past forms; the Indonesian no-tense trap ('Sales fall in 2020') is common: past years → past simple.

Prepositions and degree. to = the new level (rose to 800), by = the size of the change (rose by 3 million), from … to … (from 400 to 800), at = a point or a top (peaked at 400, remained stable at about 300), between = the range (fluctuated between 38,000 and 70,000). The node's common error *'increased until 20%' (from Indonesian 'sampai'): until is for TIME (remained stable until 2024), never for a level. Nouns: a rise / an increase / a fall / a peak; a rise IN + what changed (a rise in sales), a rise OF + the amount (a rise of 20%). Degree: verb + adverb (rose sharply) ↔ There was a + adjective + noun (a sharp rise). Big: dramatically, sharply, significantly, considerably; slow and regular: steadily, gradually; small: slightly. Don't test percentage vs percentage points (from 20% to 25% is strictly 'by 5 percentage points'); test 'by' with ordinary amounts (users, cups, rupiah).

Comparing figures (builds on as … as from A2). Multiples: twice as high as, three times as many as, half as much as (twice / three times / half + as … as). 'twice higher than' is a common learner form that examiners mark down: teach twice as high as. 'three times more than' is common and widely accepted, but 'three times as many as' is the safest: accept both, don't test the difference. Indonesian trap: 'dua kali lipat' = twice as high as / doubled, not *'two times higher'. Degree before a comparative: slightly / a little (small difference), much / far / significantly (big): slightly lower than, much higher than. Superlatives: the highest, the lowest, the second highest. Approximation: about, approximately, roughly, nearly / almost (a bit less), just over / just under. Fractions: a quarter (25%), a third (about 33%), half (50%), three quarters (75%), the majority / a small minority. many / the number of + countable (users, cups) vs much / the amount of + uncountable (water, money). Don't test 'compared with', 'in contrast' or 'respectively'; accept them if used correctly.

IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 (about 20 minutes, at least 150 words; Task 2 is the essay and counts for more). Four paragraphs: 1) introduction: one sentence that says what the chart shows, where and when, in your own words (paraphrase; don't copy the task); 2) overview: Overall, + the two or three main trends or biggest features, with no (or almost no) numbers: a report without an overview can't get a high score; 3–4) two body paragraphs that GROUP the features (e.g. the two drinks that went up vs the one that went up and down), with selected numbers and comparisons, not every figure. No opinion, no reasons or guesses about why (*'This was probably because…'), no new information, no conclusion that gives an opinion. Tenses: The table shows … (present simple) + past simple for past years. The General Training Task 1 is a letter, not taught here.

Grammar limits: A0–B1 grammar + the chain. No participle clauses (*rising to 800, reaching a peak of*), no non-defining relatives (*…, which was the highest*), no future forms for predictions (is expected to): IELTS model answers often use them; if a learner uses them correctly, accept them and say they're for later. Free writing feedback: praise the shape first, then correct one or two things only, usually a missing overview, numbers in the overview, an opinion or a reason, listing every figure, 'was increase' or 'until 20%'. Count words between spaces (numbers count as words); under 150 loses marks.

keyPoints.title: Trend words: rise, fall, peak, level off, fluctuate
keyPoints.explanation: Up: rise (rose), increase, grow (grew), go up (went up). Down: fall (fell), decrease, decline, drop. Top: peak at. Flat: level off, remain stable. Up and down: fluctuate. A chart line moves by itself, so use the active: 'The number of users increased', never 'was increase'. Use to for the new level (rose to 800), by for the size of the change (rose by 300), from … to …, and never until with a number. Say how much with an adverb after the verb (rose sharply) or an adjective before a noun (a sharp rise in sales).

examples.en: Sales rose to 800 cups a day in 2024.
examples.id: Penjualan naik menjadi 800 cangkir per hari pada 2024.

examples.en: Juice sales peaked at 400 cups in 2022.
examples.id: Penjualan jus mencapai puncaknya di 400 cangkir pada 2022.

examples.en: There was a sharp rise in online sales.
examples.id: Ada kenaikan tajam dalam penjualan online.

id.title: Kata-kata tren: rise, fall, peak, level off, fluctuate
id.explanation: Naik: rise (rose), increase, grow (grew), go up (went up). Turun: fall (fell), decrease, decline, drop. Puncak: peak at. Datar: level off, remain stable. Naik-turun: fluctuate. Garis grafik bergerak sendiri, jadi pakai bentuk aktif: 'The number of users increased', jangan pernah 'was increase'. Pakai to untuk level barunya (rose to 800), by untuk besarnya perubahan (rose by 300), from … to …, dan jangan pakai until dengan angka. Katakan seberapa besar dengan kata keterangan setelah kata kerja (rose sharply) atau kata sifat sebelum kata benda (a sharp rise in sales).

keyPoints.title: Comparing figures: twice as high as, slightly lower than
keyPoints.explanation: For multiples, put the number word before as … as: twice as high as, three times as many as, half as much as (not 'twice higher than'). Say how big the difference is before a comparative: slightly lower than (a small difference), much higher than (a big one). Use the highest / the second highest for the top, and about, roughly, nearly, just over and fractions (a quarter, a third, half) when the figure isn't round.

examples.en: Coffee sales were twice as high as tea sales.
examples.id: Penjualan kopi dua kali lipat penjualan teh.

examples.en: Ticket prices in May were slightly lower than in April.
examples.id: Harga tiket di bulan Mei sedikit lebih rendah daripada di bulan April.

examples.en: Just over a third of the students cycle to campus.
examples.id: Sedikit lebih dari sepertiga mahasiswa bersepeda ke kampus.

id.title: Membandingkan angka: twice as high as, slightly lower than
id.explanation: Untuk kelipatan, taruh kata bilangannya sebelum as … as: twice as high as, three times as many as, half as much as (bukan 'twice higher than'). Katakan seberapa besar bedanya sebelum bentuk perbandingan: slightly lower than (beda kecil), much higher than (beda besar). Pakai the highest / the second highest untuk yang paling atas, dan about, roughly, nearly, just over serta pecahan (a quarter, a third, half) kalau angkanya tidak bulat.

keyPoints.title: An IELTS Task 1 graph report in four paragraphs
keyPoints.explanation: Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. 1) Introduction: what the chart shows, where and when, in your own words. 2) Overview: Overall, + the main trends, with no numbers. 3–4) Two body paragraphs that group the features, with selected numbers and comparisons. Only report what the chart shows: no opinion and no reasons why.

examples.en: The table shows how many cups of three drinks a café chain sold per day between 2019 and 2024.
examples.id: Tabel ini menunjukkan berapa cangkir tiga jenis minuman yang terjual per hari di sebuah jaringan kafe antara 2019 dan 2024.

examples.en: Overall, coffee was the most popular drink, and its sales rose considerably.
examples.id: Secara keseluruhan, kopi adalah minuman paling laris, dan penjualannya naik cukup besar.

examples.en: Tea sales remained stable at about 300 cups a day for the whole period.
examples.id: Penjualan teh tetap stabil di sekitar 300 cangkir per hari sepanjang periode itu.

id.title: Laporan grafik IELTS Task 1 dalam empat paragraf
id.explanation: Tulis minimal 150 kata dalam sekitar 20 menit. 1) Pendahuluan: apa yang ditunjukkan grafiknya, di mana dan kapan, dengan kata-katamu sendiri. 2) Overview (gambaran umum): Overall, + tren-tren utama, tanpa angka. 3–4) Dua paragraf isi yang mengelompokkan ciri-cirinya, dengan angka pilihan dan perbandingan. Laporkan hanya apa yang ditunjukkan grafiknya: tanpa opini dan tanpa alasan kenapa.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the past simple of these three trend verbs: rise, fall, grow.
expected: rose fell grew
rose, fell, grew
guidedPractice.hint: All three are irregular: rise → r_se, fall → f_ll, grow → gr_w.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The price of cooking oil increased until Rp20,000 a litre in March.
expected: the price of cooking oil increased to rp20,000 a litre in march
the price of cooking oil increased to rp20000 a litre in march
the price of cooking oil rose to rp20,000 a litre in march
guidedPractice.hint: Rp20,000 is the new level, so use to. until is only for time (until March).

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite with a noun: The price of rice rose slightly in 2024. → There was ___ in the price of rice in 2024.
expected: a slight rise
a slight increase
guidedPractice.hint: rose slightly (verb + adverb) → a slight rise (a + adjective + noun).

guidedPractice.prompt: A warung sold 900 portions of nasi goreng and 300 portions of mie goreng last month. Complete: It sold ___ as many portions of nasi goreng as mie goreng.
expected: three times
guidedPractice.hint: 900 ÷ 300 = 3. The number word goes before as … as.

guidedPractice.prompt: In an IELTS Task 1 report, what do we call the paragraph that gives the main trends without numbers? (one word)
expected: overview
the overview
an overview
guidedPractice.hint: It usually comes second and starts with Overall,.

independentPractice.prompt: In a survey, 20% of office workers in Depok and 40% in Bogor said they take the KRL to work (practice figures). Write one sentence that compares the two figures with half.
expected: the figure for depok was half as high as the figure for bogor
the percentage for depok was half as high as the percentage for bogor
the figure for depok was half the figure for bogor
the percentage of workers in depok who take the krl was half as high as in bogor
independentPractice.hint: half + as high as: The figure for Depok was half as high as …

independentPractice.prompt: Describe this trend in one sentence with peak: visitors to a beach in Lombok (practice figures): 2021: 2,000 · 2022: 6,000 · 2023: 4,000.
expected: the number of visitors peaked at 6000 in 2022
the number of visitors peaked at 6,000 in 2022
the number of visitors reached a peak of 6000 in 2022
visitor numbers peaked at 6000 in 2022
the number of visitors rose to a peak of 6000 in 2022
independentPractice.hint: peaked at + the number + in + the year, or reached a peak of + the number.

independentPractice.prompt: Write an IELTS Task 1 report of at least 150 words. The table shows monthly users (millions) of three apps in a survey (practice figures). Ride app: 2018: 4 · 2020: 2 · 2022: 6 · 2024: 7. Food delivery app: 1 · 5 · 6 · 6. Payment app: 2 · 3 · 5 · 9. Checklist: introduction in your own words; overview with Overall, and no numbers; two body paragraphs that group the apps; trend verbs with to / by / from … to; at least two comparisons; no opinion, no reasons.
expected: the table shows the number of monthly users of three apps a ride app a food delivery app and a payment app between 2018 and 2024 overall all three apps had more users in 2024 than in 2018 and the payment app grew the most the food delivery app grew quickly at first but then levelled off in 2018 the ride app was the most popular with 4 million users a month this figure fell to 2 million in 2020 but it then rose again and reached 7 million in 2024 the payment app started with only 2 million users but it grew steadily throughout the period by 2024 it had 9 million users and it was the most popular of the three the food delivery app followed a different pattern its users rose sharply from 1 million in 2018 to 5 million in 2020 five times as many as two years before after that the number levelled off and remained stable at about 6 million until 2024
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: introduction (paraphrase, what/where/when) · overview (Overall, + 2–3 main trends, no numbers) · body 1 and body 2 grouped (e.g. ride + payment app vs food app) · accurate trend verbs and prepositions (to / by / from … to, peaked at, levelled off) · comparisons (the most popular, five times as many as) · at least 150 words · no opinion, no reasons, no conclusion with an opinion.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in this sentence from a report: The number of passengers on the MRT was increase in 2023.
acceptableAnswers: the number of passengers on the mrt increased in 2023
the number of passengers on the mrt rose in 2023
the number of passengers on the mrt went up in 2023
the number of passengers on the mrt grew in 2023
in 2023 the number of passengers on the mrt increased
in 2023 the number of passengers on the mrt rose
in 2023 the number of passengers on the mrt went up
in 2023 the number of passengers on the mrt grew
assessment.rubric: Correct: The number of passengers on the MRT increased in 2023 (active past simple: a number goes up by itself, so no passive and no 'was'). rose / went up / grew = 100. 'was increased' = 30 (a passive: it means someone increased it). 'increase' or 'increases' = 30 (no past tense for 2023). Unchanged 'was increase' = 0.

assessment.prompt: The table shows the monthly users of a food delivery app in Surabaya (practice figures): January: 2 million · June: 5 million. Write the missing preposition (one word): Between January and June, the number of users grew ___ 3 million.
assessment.rubric: Correct: by (3 million is the size of the change: 5 − 2 = 3). 'to' = 0 (to gives the new level, which was 5 million, not 3). 'until' = 0 (until is for time, never for a number). 'of' = 20 (a rise OF 3 million is right with the noun, not after the verb grew).

assessment.prompt: The table shows the price of red chillies per kilo at a market in Jakarta (practice figures): Jan: Rp40,000 · Feb: Rp65,000 · Mar: Rp38,000 · Apr: Rp70,000 · May: Rp45,000. Write the trend verb in the past simple that means 'went up and down many times': Between January and May, the price ___ between Rp38,000 and Rp70,000.
assessment.rubric: Correct: fluctuated (the price went up and down again and again, between a low and a high). 'varied' or 'ranged' = 70 (grammatical with between, but they don't show the ups and downs). 'fluctuate' = 50 (right word, no past tense). 'rose', 'fell', 'peaked' or 'levelled off' = 0 (one direction only).

assessment.prompt: A café in Yogyakarta sold 600 cups of kopi susu and 300 cups of tea last Saturday. Write the missing word (one word): Sales of kopi susu were ___ as high as sales of tea.
assessment.rubric: Correct: twice (600 is 2 × 300; twice + as high as). 'two times' = 80 (understood, but twice is the normal word). 'double' = 30 ('double the sales of tea' is possible, but not before as … as). 'more' or 'higher' = 0 (they can't go before as … as).

assessment.prompt: In a survey of 200 students at a campus in Malang, 52 said they walk to class (26%). Complete with a fraction (two words): Just over ___ of the students walk to class.
assessment.rubric: Correct: a quarter (25%; 26% is just over it). 'one quarter' = 100. 'a fourth' = 100 (American English). 'a third' = 0 (about 33%). 'half' = 0 (50%).

assessment.prompt: This body paragraph is from an IELTS Task 1 report about cinema tickets in a city. One sentence doesn't belong in this kind of report. Write its number. '(1) In 2019, the city's cinemas sold about 50,000 tickets a month. (2) This figure fell sharply to 5,000 in 2020. (3) This was probably because people were afraid of the virus. (4) Sales then rose steadily and reached 45,000 in 2024.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 3 (it gives a reason, a guess about why: an IELTS Task 1 report only describes what the chart shows). 1, 2 or 4 = 0 (they report figures and trends from the chart).

assessment.prompt: Here are four parts of an IELTS Task 1 report about how buyers in a survey paid for online shopping, mixed up. Put them in the order taught in this lesson (introduction, then overview, then details) and write the four letters. A: In 2019, 60% of buyers paid by bank transfer, but this figure fell to 20% in 2024. B: The line graph shows how buyers in a survey paid for online shopping between 2019 and 2024. C: Overall, bank transfers became much less common, while e-wallets became the most popular way to pay. D: However, the share of buyers who paid by e-wallet rose from 25% to 65% over the same period.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B C A D (B = introduction: what, who, when; C = overview: Overall, + the main trends, no numbers; A = details on bank transfers; D = However, points back to A and gives the opposite trend). 'B A D C' = 70 (IELTS also accepts the overview at the end, but the lesson's order puts it second). 'B C D A' = 40 (D's However has nothing to contrast with). Any order that doesn't start with B = 0.

material.title: Up, down, top, flat, up and down: trend words

blocks.text:
A **trend** is the direction a figure moves over time: up, down, flat, or up and down. A chart in IELTS or a work report usually shows a line, bars or a table. **The app can't show you a real picture here, so every chart in this lesson is a small table of figures** (all of them practice figures, not real statistics).

The five families of trend words:
- **Up:** *rise* (rose, risen), *increase*, *grow* (grew, grown), *go up* (went up)
- **Down:** *fall* (fell, fallen), *decrease*, *decline*, *drop*
- **The top:** *peak* (peaked at 400) / *reach a peak* (of 400)
- **Flat:** *level off* (stop rising or falling), *remain stable* / *remain steady*
- **Up and down many times:** *fluctuate* (fluctuated between 38,000 and 70,000)

The chart shows the past, so most verbs are in the **past simple**. Careful: **rise, fall** and **grow** are irregular.

id.text:
**Tren** adalah arah gerak sebuah angka dari waktu ke waktu: naik, turun, datar, atau naik-turun. Grafik di IELTS atau laporan kantor biasanya berupa garis, batang atau tabel. **Aplikasi ini tidak bisa menampilkan gambar grafik asli di sini, jadi setiap grafik di pelajaran ini berupa tabel angka kecil** (semuanya angka latihan, bukan statistik asli).

Lima kelompok kata tren:
- **Naik:** *rise* (rose, risen), *increase*, *grow* (grew, grown), *go up* (went up)
- **Turun:** *fall* (fell, fallen), *decrease*, *decline*, *drop*
- **Puncak:** *peak* (peaked at 400) / *reach a peak* (of 400)
- **Datar:** *level off* (berhenti naik atau turun), *remain stable* / *remain steady*
- **Naik-turun berkali-kali:** *fluctuate* (fluctuated between 38,000 and 70,000)

Grafiknya menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi kebanyakan kata kerjanya memakai **past simple** (bentuk lampau). Hati-hati: **rise, fall** dan **grow** tidak beraturan.

rows.en: The number of online shoppers rose every year.
rows.id: Jumlah pembeli online naik setiap tahun.

id.note: naik: rise → rose (tidak beraturan)

rows.en: Ticket sales fell in 2020.
rows.id: Penjualan tiket turun pada 2020.

id.note: turun: fall → fell (tidak beraturan)

rows.en: Juice sales peaked at 400 cups in 2022.
rows.id: Penjualan jus mencapai puncaknya di 400 cangkir pada 2022.
rows.note: the top: peak at + the highest number

id.note: puncak: peak at + angka tertinggi

rows.en: After 2022, the number of users levelled off.
rows.id: Setelah 2022, jumlah pengguna mulai mendatar.

id.note: datar: Inggris British levelled, Amerika leveled

rows.en: Tea sales remained stable at about 300 cups a day.
rows.id: Penjualan teh tetap stabil di sekitar 300 cangkir per hari.

id.note: datar dalam waktu lama

rows.en: The price of chillies fluctuated all year.
rows.id: Harga cabai naik-turun sepanjang tahun.

id.note: naik-turun berkali-kali

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **no** ***was*** **for** ***sudah***. *Jumlah pengguna sudah meningkat* is not `The number of users was increase`: the past is already in *-ed*. And not `was increased` either: a figure goes up **by itself**, so use the plain past: **The number of users increased.** (*was increased* would mean someone increased it on purpose, like *The company increased its prices*.) Also **rise** vs **raise**: *naik* = **rise** (prices rose), *menaikkan* = **raise** + something (the shop raised its prices).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **tidak ada** ***was*** **untuk** ***sudah***. *Jumlah pengguna sudah meningkat* bukan `The number of users was increase`: makna lampaunya sudah ada di *-ed*. Juga bukan `was increased`: angka naik **dengan sendirinya**, jadi pakai bentuk lampau biasa: **The number of users increased.** (*was increased* berarti ada orang yang sengaja menaikkannya, seperti *The company increased its prices*.) Juga **rise** vs **raise**: *naik* = **rise** (prices rose), *menaikkan* = **raise** + sesuatu (the shop raised its prices).

blocks.prompt: A food app had 5,000 users in January, 9,000 in April and 9,000 in July. Which verb describes April to July?
blocks.explain: From April to July the figure didn't change (9,000 → 9,000), so it **remained stable**. *fluctuated* means up and down many times, and *peaked* is for a top followed by a fall.

id.prompt: Sebuah aplikasi makanan punya 5.000 pengguna di bulan Januari, 9.000 di April dan 9.000 di Juli. Kata kerja mana yang menggambarkan April sampai Juli?
id.explain: Dari April sampai Juli angkanya tidak berubah (9.000 → 9.000), jadi **remained stable**. *fluctuated* berarti naik-turun berkali-kali, dan *peaked* untuk titik tertinggi yang setelahnya turun.

id.title: Naik, turun, puncak, datar, naik-turun: kata-kata tren

material.title: How far and how fast: to, by, from … to, sharply, a sharp rise

blocks.text:
Small words carry big meaning with numbers:
- **to** + the **new level**: *Sales rose **to** 800 cups.* (the line ends at 800)
- **by** + the **size of the change**: *Sales rose **by** 300 cups.* (500 → 800: the difference)
- **from … to …**: *Sales rose **from** 500 **to** 800 cups.*
- **at** + a point: *peaked **at** 400*, *remained stable **at** about 300*
- **between** + a range: *fluctuated **between** Rp38,000 **and** Rp70,000*

To say **how much or how fast**, use an **adverb** (kata keterangan, usually -ly) after the verb, or an **adjective** (kata sifat) before a **noun** (kata benda):
- *Sales **rose sharply**.* = *There was **a sharp rise** in sales.*
- big: *sharply, dramatically, significantly, considerably*
- slow and regular: *steadily, gradually*
- small: *slightly*

With the nouns, **a rise in** + what changed (*a rise in sales*), **a rise of** + the amount (*a rise of 300 cups*).

id.text:
Kata-kata kecil membawa arti besar dalam angka:
- **to** + **level barunya**: *Sales rose **to** 800 cups.* (garisnya berakhir di 800)
- **by** + **besarnya perubahan**: *Sales rose **by** 300 cups.* (500 → 800: selisihnya)
- **from … to …**: *Sales rose **from** 500 **to** 800 cups.*
- **at** + satu titik: *peaked **at** 400*, *remained stable **at** about 300*
- **between** + rentang: *fluctuated **between** Rp38,000 **and** Rp70,000*

Untuk mengatakan **seberapa banyak atau seberapa cepat**, pakai **kata keterangan** (adverb, biasanya berakhiran -ly) setelah kata kerja, atau **kata sifat** (adjective) sebelum **kata benda** (noun):
- *Sales **rose sharply**.* = *There was **a sharp rise** in sales.*
- besar: *sharply, dramatically, significantly, considerably*
- pelan dan teratur: *steadily, gradually*
- kecil: *slightly*

Dengan kata benda, **a rise in** + apa yang berubah (*a rise in sales*), **a rise of** + jumlahnya (*a rise of 300 cups*).

rows.en: The number of members rose from 500 to 800.
rows.id: Jumlah anggota naik dari 500 menjadi 800.
rows.note: from … to …: where it started and ended

id.note: from … to …: titik awal dan akhirnya

rows.en: In other words, it rose by 300.
rows.id: Dengan kata lain, jumlahnya naik sebanyak 300.

id.note: by = selisihnya (800 − 500)

rows.en: Online sales increased dramatically in 2020.
rows.id: Penjualan online meningkat drastis pada 2020.

id.note: kata kerja + kata keterangan

rows.en: There was a dramatic increase in online sales in 2020.
rows.id: Ada peningkatan drastis dalam penjualan online pada 2020.
rows.note: a + adjective + noun, then in + what changed

id.note: a + kata sifat + kata benda, lalu in + apa yang berubah

rows.en: The number of users remained stable until 2024.
rows.id: Jumlah pengguna tetap stabil sampai 2024.

id.note: until + waktu itu benar

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: ***sampai*** **with a number is not** ***until***. *Naik sampai 20%* → *rose **to** 20%* (the new level) or *rose **by** 20%* (the size of the change), never `increased until 20%`. **until** is only for **time**: *remained stable until 2024*. And watch the meaning: from 500 to 800 is *rose **to** 800* but *rose **by** 300*.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: ***sampai*** **dengan angka bukan** ***until***. *Naik sampai 20%* → *rose **to** 20%* (level barunya) atau *rose **by** 20%* (besarnya perubahan), jangan pernah `increased until 20%`. **until** hanya untuk **waktu**: *remained stable until 2024*. Dan perhatikan artinya: dari 500 ke 800 itu *rose **to** 800* tetapi *rose **by** 300*.

blocks.prompt: The price of a bottle of water at a campus canteen went from Rp3,000 to Rp5,000. Complete: The price rose ___ Rp2,000.
blocks.explain: Rp2,000 is the **size of the change** (5,000 − 3,000), so use **by**. *to* would give the new level (Rp5,000), and *until* is only for time.

id.prompt: Harga sebotol air di kantin kampus berubah dari Rp3.000 menjadi Rp5.000. Lengkapi: The price rose ___ Rp2,000.
id.explain: Rp2.000 adalah **besarnya perubahan** (5.000 − 3.000), jadi pakai **by**. *to* untuk level barunya (Rp5.000), dan *until* hanya untuk waktu.

id.title: Seberapa jauh dan seberapa cepat: to, by, from … to, sharply, a sharp rise

material.title: Comparing figures: twice as high as, slightly lower than, a quarter

blocks.text:
Quick recap from A2: **bigger than**, **more expensive than**, **the biggest**, **as big as**. With figures you go one step further and say **how much** bigger.
- **Multiples:** put *twice*, *three times* or *half* **before as … as**: *twice as high as*, *three times as many as*, *half as much as*.
- **How big the difference is:** a word **before** the comparative: *slightly / a little* lower than (small), *much / far / significantly* higher than (big).
- **The top and the bottom:** *the highest*, *the lowest*, *the second highest*.
- **Figures that aren't round:** *about, approximately, roughly* (more or less), *nearly / almost* (a bit less), *just over / just under*.
- **Fractions:** *a quarter* = 25%, *a third* ≈ 33%, *half* = 50%, *three quarters* = 75%; *the majority* = more than half.

**many / the number of** + things you can count (*users, cups*), **much / the amount of** + things you can't count (*water, money*): *three times as **many** users*, *twice as **much** money*.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari A2: **bigger than**, **more expensive than**, **the biggest**, **as big as**. Dengan angka, kamu melangkah lebih jauh dan mengatakan **seberapa** lebih besar.
- **Kelipatan:** taruh *twice*, *three times* atau *half* **sebelum as … as**: *twice as high as* (dua kali lipat), *three times as many as* (tiga kali lipat), *half as much as* (setengahnya).
- **Seberapa besar bedanya:** satu kata **sebelum** bentuk perbandingan: *slightly / a little* lower than (sedikit), *much / far / significantly* higher than (jauh).
- **Paling atas dan paling bawah:** *the highest*, *the lowest*, *the second highest* (tertinggi kedua).
- **Angka yang tidak bulat:** *about, approximately, roughly* (kurang lebih), *nearly / almost* (hampir, sedikit kurang), *just over / just under* (sedikit di atas / sedikit di bawah).
- **Pecahan:** *a quarter* = 25% (seperempat), *a third* ≈ 33% (sepertiga), *half* = 50% (setengah), *three quarters* = 75%; *the majority* = lebih dari setengah.

**many / the number of** + benda yang bisa dihitung (*users, cups*), **much / the amount of** + benda yang tidak bisa dihitung (*water, money*): *three times as **many** users*, *twice as **much** money*.

rows.id: Cabang Jakarta punya pelanggan tiga kali lipat cabang Bogor.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: ***dua kali lipat*** → **twice as high as** (or *doubled*), not `two times higher than` or `twice higher than`. Keep the pattern **number word + as … as**. Also don't mix the A2 rules: `more higher` (higher already means *lebih tinggi*) and `lower from` (it's **than**). And *three times more than* is common and many people accept it, but *three times as many as* is always safe.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: ***dua kali lipat*** → **twice as high as** (atau *doubled*), bukan `two times higher than` atau `twice higher than`. Pegang polanya: **kata bilangan + as … as**. Jangan campur aturan A2 juga: `more higher` (higher sudah berarti *lebih tinggi*) dan `lower from` (yang benar **than**). *three times more than* juga sering dipakai dan banyak orang menerimanya, tetapi *three times as many as* selalu aman.

blocks.prompt: Branch A sold 1,200 phones and Branch B sold 400. Which sentence is correct?
options: Branch A sold three times as many phones as Branch B.
Branch A sold three times as much phones as Branch B.
Branch A sold three times more many phones than Branch B.
blocks.explain: 1,200 is 3 × 400, and phones can be counted, so **three times as many … as**. *much* is for things you can't count, and *more many … than* mixes two patterns.

id.prompt: Cabang A menjual 1.200 HP dan Cabang B menjual 400. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: 1.200 adalah 3 × 400, dan HP bisa dihitung, jadi **three times as many … as**. *much* untuk benda yang tidak bisa dihitung, dan *more many … than* mencampur dua pola.

material.title: The IELTS Writing Task 1 report: four paragraphs, 150+ words

blocks.text:
In **IELTS Academic Writing Task 1** you get a chart (a line graph, bar chart, pie chart or table) and you have about **20 minutes** to write **at least 150 words**. (Task 2 is the essay, and it counts for more.) The usual plan:
1. **Introduction** (1 sentence): what the chart shows, where and when, **in your own words**: *The graph shows* → *The table illustrates*; *from 2019 to 2024* → *between 2019 and 2024*.
2. **Overview** (1–2 sentences): **Overall,** + the 2–3 **main trends** or biggest features, with **no numbers**. Examiners look for it: without an overview, a report can't get a high score.
3–4. **Two body paragraphs**: **group** the features (the lines that went up vs the one that went up and down), with **selected** numbers and comparisons. Don't list every figure.

**Only report what the chart shows**: no opinion (*I think*), no reasons or guesses about **why** (*This was probably because…*), and no conclusion with an opinion. Use *The table shows* (present) + the **past simple** for past years.

Here's a full report (165 words). The chart, as a table: cups sold per day at a café chain in Bandung (practice figures).
- Coffee: 2019: 400 · 2020: 350 · 2021: 450 · 2022: 600 · 2023: 750 · 2024: 800
- Tea: 300 · 300 · 300 · 310 · 290 · 300
- Fruit juice: 100 · 150 · 250 · 400 · 250 · 200

id.text:
Di **IELTS Academic Writing Task 1** kamu mendapat grafik (grafik garis, diagram batang, diagram lingkaran atau tabel) dan punya sekitar **20 menit** untuk menulis **minimal 150 kata**. (Task 2 adalah esai, dan nilainya lebih besar.) Susunan yang biasa:
1. **Pendahuluan** (1 kalimat): apa yang ditunjukkan grafiknya, di mana dan kapan, **dengan kata-katamu sendiri** (parafrase): *The graph shows* → *The table illustrates*; *from 2019 to 2024* → *between 2019 and 2024*.
2. **Overview** (gambaran umum, 1–2 kalimat): **Overall,** + 2–3 **tren utama** atau ciri paling menonjol, **tanpa angka**. Penguji mencarinya: tanpa overview, laporanmu tidak bisa dapat nilai tinggi.
3–4. **Dua paragraf isi**: **kelompokkan** ciri-cirinya (garis yang naik vs yang naik-turun), dengan angka **pilihan** dan perbandingan. Jangan sebutkan semua angka.

**Laporkan hanya apa yang ditunjukkan grafiknya**: tanpa opini (*I think*), tanpa alasan atau tebakan **kenapa** (*This was probably because…*), dan tanpa kesimpulan berisi opini. Pakai *The table shows* (present) + **past simple** untuk tahun-tahun yang sudah lewat.

Ini contoh laporan lengkap (165 kata). Grafiknya, dalam bentuk tabel: cangkir yang terjual per hari di sebuah jaringan kafe di Bandung (angka latihan).
- Coffee: 2019: 400 · 2020: 350 · 2021: 450 · 2022: 600 · 2023: 750 · 2024: 800
- Tea: 300 · 300 · 300 · 310 · 290 · 300
- Fruit juice: 100 · 150 · 250 · 400 · 250 · 200

rows.en: The table shows how many cups of coffee, tea and fruit juice a café chain in Bandung sold per day between 2019 and 2024.
rows.id: Tabel ini menunjukkan berapa cangkir kopi, teh dan jus buah yang terjual per hari di sebuah jaringan kafe di Bandung antara 2019 dan 2024.
rows.note: paragraph 1 · introduction: what, where, when, in your own words

id.note: paragraf 1 · pendahuluan: apa, di mana, kapan, dengan kata-katamu sendiri

rows.en: Overall, coffee was the most popular drink throughout the period, and its sales rose considerably. Tea sales hardly changed, whereas juice sales rose and then fell again.
rows.id: Secara keseluruhan, kopi adalah minuman paling laris sepanjang periode itu, dan penjualannya naik cukup besar. Penjualan teh hampir tidak berubah, sedangkan penjualan jus naik lalu turun lagi.
rows.note: paragraph 2 · overview: the main trends, no numbers

id.note: paragraf 2 · overview (gambaran umum): tren utama, tanpa angka

rows.en: In 2019, the chain sold 400 cups of coffee a day. This figure fell slightly to 350 in 2020, but it then rose steadily and reached 800 cups in 2024, twice as many as in 2019. Tea sales remained stable at about 300 cups a day for the whole period. By 2024, coffee sales were almost three times as high as tea sales.
rows.id: Pada 2019, jaringan kafe itu menjual 400 cangkir kopi per hari. Angka ini sedikit turun menjadi 350 pada 2020, tetapi kemudian naik terus dengan stabil dan mencapai 800 cangkir pada 2024, dua kali lipat dari 2019. Penjualan teh tetap stabil di sekitar 300 cangkir per hari sepanjang periode. Pada 2024, penjualan kopi hampir tiga kali lipat penjualan teh.
rows.note: paragraph 3 · body 1: coffee and tea, with numbers and comparisons

id.note: paragraf 3 · isi 1: kopi dan teh, dengan angka dan perbandingan

rows.en: Juice sales followed a different pattern. They started at only 100 cups a day in 2019, but they grew rapidly and peaked at 400 cups in 2022. After that, they fell sharply to 200 cups in 2024. Nevertheless, the final figure was still twice as high as the figure for 2019.
rows.id: Penjualan jus punya pola yang berbeda. Awalnya hanya 100 cangkir per hari pada 2019, tetapi naik dengan cepat dan mencapai puncak 400 cangkir pada 2022. Setelah itu, penjualannya turun tajam menjadi 200 cangkir pada 2024. Meskipun begitu, angka terakhirnya masih dua kali lipat angka 2019.
rows.note: paragraph 4 · body 2: juice, the different pattern

id.note: paragraf 4 · isi 2: jus, polanya yang berbeda

blocks.text: Indonesian school reports often end with *Kesimpulannya, menurut saya…* or explain *karena…*. In IELTS Task 1 that loses marks: **describe, don't explain**. And count your words: numbers count as words, and under 150 words loses marks. British vs American: *levelled off / leveled off*, *per cent / percent*: choose one and keep it.

id.text: Laporan di sekolah Indonesia sering ditutup dengan *Kesimpulannya, menurut saya…* atau menjelaskan *karena…*. Di IELTS Task 1 itu mengurangi nilai: **deskripsikan, jangan jelaskan**. Dan hitung kata-katamu: angka juga dihitung sebagai kata, dan kurang dari 150 kata mengurangi nilai. Inggris British vs Amerika: *levelled off / leveled off*, *per cent / percent*: pilih satu dan konsisten.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence should NOT be in an IELTS Task 1 report about the café chain?
options: This was probably because coffee shops became fashionable.
Juice sales peaked at 400 cups in 2022.
blocks.explain: The middle sentence gives a **reason** (a guess about why). Task 1 only **describes** what the chart shows; the other two report trends from the table.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang TIDAK boleh ada di laporan IELTS Task 1 tentang jaringan kafe itu?
id.explain: Kalimat tengah memberi **alasan** (tebakan kenapa). Task 1 hanya **mendeskripsikan** apa yang ditunjukkan grafiknya; dua kalimat lainnya melaporkan tren dari tabel.

flashcards.back: rise (rose, risen) / increase / grow (grew) / go up (went up): Sales rose.
fall (fell, fallen) / decrease / decline / drop: Ticket sales fell in 2020.
peak at 400 · level off / remain stable · fluctuate between X and Y

flashcards.front: naik sampai 20% (level baru) vs naik sebanyak 20 (selisih)
flashcards.back: rose to 20% (new level) vs rose by 20 (the change) · never 'until 20%'

flashcards.front: naik tajam (kata kerja) vs kenaikan tajam (kata benda)
flashcards.back: rose sharply · There was a sharp rise in sales.
twice as high as / twice as many as · half as much as (not 'twice higher than')
slightly lower than (small difference) · much higher than (big difference)
introduction → overview (Overall, no numbers) → body 1 → body 2 · 150+ words · no opinion, no reasons

id.note: Contoh teks B2 yang membandingkan dua diagram lingkaran (cara orang memakai smartphone dan tablet), dengan tips memilih angka yang paling penting dan menghubungkan persamaan serta perbedaan (while, however). Perbandingannya kebanyakan memakai persentase, bukan twice as … as.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa membandingkan (**bigger than**, **as … as**) dan menghubungkan ide (**whereas**, **Nevertheless,**, **Overall,**). Sekarang kamu memakainya untuk angka: mengatakan bagaimana angka **naik, turun, mencapai puncak** dan **naik-turun**, membandingkannya dengan tepat (**twice as high as**, **slightly lower than**), dan menulis laporan grafik ala **IELTS Writing Task 1**. Aplikasi ini tidak bisa menampilkan grafik asli di sini, jadi setiap grafik diberikan sebagai tabel angka kecil.

assessment.dd-7: Ini empat bagian laporan IELTS Task 1 tentang cara pembeli dalam sebuah survei membayar belanja online, tapi urutannya teracak. Susun sesuai urutan di pelajaran ini (pendahuluan, lalu overview, lalu detail) dan tulis keempat hurufnya. A: In 2019, 60% of buyers paid by bank transfer, but this figure fell to 20% in 2024.
